changelog: - **A Converter taking from Pools no longer loses resources without a trace, and two connections into one target share its room.** A Converter now decides how much of its recipe it can run before it takes anything from its Pools, so it never takes more than it can turn into output, and every one of its Pool connections moves the same share of the recipe. Two Converter outputs into the same Pool or the same Gate, and two Gate branches into the same Pool, now share that target's room. A model where a Converter had too little output room, ran with one input short, or sent two connections into one nearly full Pool can show different numbers than before, and a Converter that feeds a Pool it also takes from is limited by the net amount. One limit stays for now: a Converter with a connection coming in from a Gate or another Converter receives what that connection delivers before its own plan is made, so it can still receive more than its recipe uses; that is the next change under the same issue. A saved Monte Carlo distribution computed before this change opens marked as from an earlier version of the engine, like one from an edited graph, until you run it again; the Workspace file now says which engine computed its distribution (`loop-workspace/2`), and an app from before this change opens such a file's graph without its saved workspace. The bundled Risky Factory demo is one such model: its Assembly Converter no longer makes half a batch from energy alone while Refined Ore is still empty, so with seed 1 the run no longer ends at step 2 (seed 9 ends at step 4), and its 500-run distribution ends 419 runs instead of 424.
